notes: Voices are macOS `say` voices verified present on the build machine.
English-only voices (Samantha, Daniel, Karen, Rishi, Moira) emit ~0.01 s
of audio when handed Chinese text, so Chinese and code-switched lines are
only ever assigned to zh-capable voices (Tingting, Meijia, Sandy zh_CN),
all of which were confirmed to read Latin script as well. The generator
hard-fails on any utterance that trims below 0.25 s, so a bad assignment
aborts the run instead of silently corrupting ground truth.
A negative `gap` means the utterance starts before the previous one ends,
which is how controlled overlap is expressed.
All text is original, neutral, meeting-like filler; no real people.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: I want to walk through the whole quarter before we open it up for questions. We started with three goals, and only two of them survived the replanning in the second month. The third goal was folded into the platform workstream because the dependencies were too tangled to separate cleanly.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: On the first goal, the ingest rewrite, we are essentially finished. Throughput is roughly four times what it was, and the error rate has stayed under one percent for six consecutive weeks. The remaining work is documentation and a small amount of cleanup in the retry logic.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: The second goal was the storage migration, and that one is more complicated. We moved about eighty percent of the data without incident, but the last twenty percent lives in a legacy format that nobody has touched in years. I would rather spend an extra sprint on it than rush a conversion we cannot verify.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: So my recommendation is that we extend the migration by one sprint, keep the ingest team on documentation for the next two weeks, and revisit the platform workstream at the start of the next quarter. That gives us a clean baseline before we take on anything new.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: Thank you for the summary. I want to respond to the storage point, because I think the risk is slightly different from how it was described. The legacy format is not the hard part; the hard part is that we have no reliable record of which rows were written by the old importer.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: We tried to reconstruct that record twice last year, and both attempts produced different answers. That tells me the reconstruction itself is not trustworthy, so an extra sprint spent on conversion will not actually reduce the uncertainty. It will just move it later in the schedule.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: What I would propose instead is that we accept the legacy partition as read only, freeze it in place, and write a small compatibility layer that serves those rows without converting them. That is maybe a week of work, and it removes the migration from the critical path entirely.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: If we do that, the quarter closes with two goals genuinely complete and one deliberately deferred with a written rationale. I think that is a much more honest position than claiming a migration finished when we cannot verify the tail of it. I am happy to write that rationale up this week.

fixtures.description: Deterministic thirty-minute three-speaker meeting for memory, cancellation and stability testing. Each speaker holds the floor for several consecutive utterances, so reference turns are meeting-shaped (tens of seconds) rather than one sentence each -- an earlier version switched speaker every 2.8 s for half an hour, which is not a meeting and which dominated every corpus-level average.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: Let's take the agenda from the top and keep each item short.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: There are three things I want to get through before we finish.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: First the ingest pipeline, then the retry budget, then the release date.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: I'd like a decision on the release date today rather than next week.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: If anyone has a blocker on any of those, raise it when we get there.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: Otherwise I'll assume we're aligned and we can move quickly.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: The ingest pipeline is on track and the backfill finished overnight.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: We processed about four hundred thousand records without an error.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: The throughput held steady once we increased the batch size.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: There is one caveat, which is that the staging cluster is smaller.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: So the production numbers will be better than what I just quoted.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: I'll have exact figures in the document by tomorrow afternoon.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: I have a question about the retry budget before we move on.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: Right now I cannot tell whether it resets per request or per connection.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: That matters a lot when a downstream service is slow but not down.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: If it is per connection we could retry far more than we intend.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: I would rather we made that explicit in the configuration.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: Otherwise someone will tune it later without knowing the difference.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: That's a fair point and I don't think it's documented anywhere.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: Let's make it per request and write that down in the same change.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: Can you take that one and open a short design note for it?

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: Keep it brief, half a page is enough for a decision like this.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: Then we don't have to revisit the question in three months.

script.speaker: SPK_A
script.text: Moving on to the release date, which is the one I care about.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: I think the release date is achievable if the scope stays fixed.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: The risk is not the engineering work, it is the review queue.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: We have two changes waiting on review that block the final build.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: If those clear this week I am comfortable committing to the date.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: If they slip past Friday then I would want to move it a week.

script.speaker: SPK_B
script.text: I would rather say that now than surprise everyone later.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: I agree with that, and I can help clear the review queue.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: I have time on Thursday and I can take both of the open changes.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: That should remove the dependency that worries me the most.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: One more thing before we close, about the documentation.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: The setup guide still references the old configuration format.

script.speaker: SPK_C
script.text: I'll fix that as part of the same change so nothing is stale.
